thread:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel swap in us-west we're seeing a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of traffic. Not sure if it's keying, replication, or batching interaction. Posting quick profiler outputs and logs below.

ravi: How big is the delta and which prefixes? total tokens affected?

alex: 18% hit-rate drop on top-10k prefixes for us-west-1; p95 latency +60ms for those requests, token cost up ~12%. Timeline: kernel swap at 1715430000, regression visible by 1715431800. Quick profiler snippet: ```
kv_apply_loop: mean_apply=120.7ms (+45ms)
cache_lookup: hit=0.62 -> 0.50
key_hash_time: avg=0.8ms (+0.35ms)
kernel_dispatch: queue_depth=32 -> 48
```

marie: Hypothesis: new kernel altered quantization path ordering which changes in-memory model bytes and therefore some cache key components (we use model-version+prefix-hash+quant-mode in key). If quant-mode bit changed between nodes, replication will produce stale keys. Can we confirm key schema on both kernels? @alex

luis: Also seeing replication apply backlog on the regional feeder: ```
replicator.apply.backlog=4000
avg_apply_latency=120ms
replicate_errors=0.2% (retries)
```
That backlog lines up with the hit-rate gap windows. Looks like fanout/backpressure -> delayed primary cache install in cold nodes.

kai: Another angle — routing policy: we routed some traffic to fallback-lowmem instances (different model variant) during the swap. Those variants normalize keys differently (they drop trailing context markers). If requests are routed back to full instances later, keys don't match and we see misses. Need consistent key normalization across variants.

devbot: deploy-bot: Canary kernel v2 deployed to us-west feeders at 1715430000 by deploy/ci (canary=20% feeders).

marie: Mitigations to try (short-term): staggered warmup + targeted priming of top-500 prefixes per region, bump local TTL for primed keys to 5m, and temporarily pause routing to fallback variants for affected routes. Mid-term: enforce uniform key normalization function in runtime and gate kernel flags that affect hash inputs.

ravi: Proposed experiment plan: 1) Rollback canary to v1 on feeders (if safe) to confirm regression revert (24h). 2) If rollback not possible, run controlled priming: push top-500 prefixes to each region and monitor hit-rate p5/p50/p95 over 2h. 3) Add a canary that preserves old key schema but uses new kernel to isolate kernel vs keying. Metrics: regional hit-rate delta, apply_latency, token_cost_per_request, replication_backlog. Thresholds: fix if hit-rate delta >10% or p95 latency >50ms.

alex: I'll own the priming script and the TTL bump. @luis can you tail replicator metrics and confirm backlog clears after priming? @marie can you validate key schema across kernel builds? We'll reconvene in 30m. :thumbsup:
